newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees 15 pct of Sibneft for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees 15 pct of Sibneft for foreigners.

text.p: Russia hopes to sell a 15 percent stake in oil company Sibneft in an investment tender, probably in late October, a privatisation official said on Friday.

Yekaterina Illyuviyeva, head of the Russian property fund's investment department, told a news conference the previously announced tender for 15 percent of Sibneft was set with foreign investors in mind.
"I think this amount is not chosen at random because it allows us to attract foreign investors," she said.
The property fund is currently holding a tender for 19 percent of OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya, one of a dozen Russian vertically integrated oil companies.
This means foreigners, who are restricted to a 15 percent stake in the company, cannot bid for the first lot.
She said details of the second tender would be announced once the results of the first due on September 20, were known.
"If things go well, the tender could be held in the last days of October," she said.
In the first tender, 858.12 million shares are on offer at 82.38 billion roubles ($15.3 million). The minimum investment is $43.48 million.
In the second tender, 677.46 million shares will be on offer. The minimum investment is $33.56 million.

Illyuviyeva said the price per share had still to be set but that it would be close to that in the first tender -- 96 roubles. The shares, which are not very liquid, trade at 300-355 roubles each, she said.
Sibneft is 51 percent state-owned. Its main production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz, of which it owns 38 percent.
ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii won a tender to manage the 51 percent stake under the government's shares-for-loans scheme late last year.
Its bid of $100.3 million was guaranteed by Bank Menatep.
Russian newspapers have speculated that NFK is a vehicle for Russian businessman Boris Berezovsky, whose interests range from car dealerships to television.
Under the scheme, the auction winners were allowed to sell the shares after September 1.
President Boris Yeltsin this week signed a decree calling for shares in strategic oil companies to remain state property until December 1988.

Sibneft President Viktor Gorodilov said he had not seen a list of firms affected by the decree but said, "I think that those companies then went through shares-for-loans or special cash auctions cannot be on the list."
NFK Chief Executive Ivan Kulakov said the company was unlikely to take part in the tender and that it was happy with its role as a consultant to Sibneft.
Privatisation officials said earlier this year they planned to sell 34 percent stakes in five major oil companies -- Sibneft, Norsi-Oil, Vostochnaya (Eastern), Onako and Sidanko.
ZAO Interros Oil won a tender for 34 percent of Sidanko on Thursday. Interros Oil is affiliated with the Interros financial-industrial group, built around the Uneximbank group.
MFK bank, backed by Uneximbank, acquired 51 percent of Sidanko at a shares-for-loans auction last year.
Illyuviyeva said the fund also planned to sell 44 percent of Russia's Central Telegraph, a communications concern, in a commercial tender but had no details.
--Nigel Stephenson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 ($ = 5378 Russian Roubles)
